note: US reference values (CDC STEADI). Not validated for Indian older adults.
source_note: Every value below was read from the primary CDC STEADI assessment PDFs (2017 sheets, hosted on cdc.gov), retrieved 2026-10-22. The 30-second chair stand table was also checked against a rendered image of the page. No state-hosted copies were used. These are US reference values for the physiotherapist to interpret. They are not diagnostic and do not predict falls.

chairStand30s.meaning: Number of full stands in 30 seconds with arms crossed on the chest. A score below the cut-off for the person's age band and sex is a 'below average score', which the CDC sheet says 'indicates a risk for falls'.

protocol.armsUsedRule: If the patient must use his/her arms to stand, stop the test. Record '0' for the number and score.
protocol.endOfWindowRule: If the patient is over halfway to a standing position when 30 seconds have elapsed, count it as a stand.

source.title: STEADI Assessment: 30-Second Chair Stand
source.publisher: CDC National Center for Injury Prevention and Control

entries.population: older adult (no age band given on the sheet)
entries.meaning: Verbatim: 'An older adult who takes >=12 seconds to complete the TUG is at risk for falling.' The sheet does not use the words 'further assessment'.

protocol.timingRule: On the word 'Go,' begin timing. Stop timing after patient sits back down.
protocol.chair: The sheet says 'sit back in a standard arm chair'.
protocol.footwearAndAids: Patients wear their regular footwear and can use a walking aid, if needed.

source.title: STEADI Assessment: Timed Up & Go (TUG)
source.publisher: CDC National Center for Injury Prevention and Control

stages.name: semi-tandem
stages.cdcText: Place the instep of one foot so it is touching the big toe of the other foot.

stages.name: tandem
stages.cdcText: Tandem stand: Place one foot in front of the other, heel touching toe.

protocol.progressionRule: If the patient can hold a position for 10 seconds without moving their feet or needing support, go on to the next position. If not, STOP the test.
protocol.allowedMovement: You can hold your arms out, or move your body to help keep your balance, but don't move your feet.
protocol.otherRules: Patients should not use an assistive device (cane or walker) and they should keep their eyes open.

source.title: STEADI Assessment: The 4-Stage Balance Test
source.publisher: CDC National Center for Injury Prevention and Control

entries.population: older adult (no age band given on the sheet)
entries.meaning: Verbatim: 'An older adult who cannot hold the tandem stand for at least 10 seconds is at increased risk of falling.'

notProvidedBySource: Chair-stand cut-offs for ages below 60 or above 94: the CDC table covers 60-64 to 90-94 only.
TUG cut-offs by age band or sex: the CDC sheet gives one value (>=12 s) for older adults.
Balance cut-offs for stages 1, 2 and 4: the CDC sheet gives a risk statement for the tandem stage only.
Any Indian reference values: none exist in the CDC sources.
urlNotes: The 4-stage balance PDF is at STEADI-Assessment-4Stage-508.pdf (found via search). The URL pattern steadi-assessment-4stagebalance-508.pdf returned 404.
Direct curl downloads from cdc.gov returned 403 (bot block). The PDFs were fetched through a web fetch tool and their text was extracted locally.
